extracted.intended_audience: Sage developers and contributors who run and maintain Sage doctests and use the doctest fixer
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for running, debugging, and updating Sage's doctests (including running under gdb/valgrind, repeating tests to find flaky failures, using the doctest fixer to update expected outputs, and testing in virtual/Docker environments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctester failure reporting / verbose output
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctest framework prints out the output so you know what test caused the problem; use the --verbose flag to have this output appear in real time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tests fail the doctester prints the output collected so far. Use --verbose for realtime prints; the first failure in a file often causes a cascade of others, so use --initial to show only the first failure in each doctest block.

rubrics_metrics.name: --gdb flag / running under gdb
rubrics_metrics.description: Run doctests under gdb to debug severe errors (segfaults/hangs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example invocation shown: ./sage -t --gdb src/sage/schemes/elliptic_curves/constructor.py which is expanded to exec gdb --eval-commands="run" --args <python> sage-runtests ...; use gdb to inspect state, backtraces, and reproduce failures interactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use valgrind tools (--valgrind / --memcheck / --massif / --cachegrind / --omega)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run doctests under valgrind tools to track down memory issues or other low-level problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sage includes valgrind; run doctests with --valgrind (or specific tools like --memcheck, --massif, --cachegrind, --omega). See Sage wiki ValgrindingSage for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: --failed / -f flag (rerun only failed files)
rubrics_metrics.description: After fixing problems, rerun just those files that failed their most recent test using the --failed flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ./sage -t -fa will doctest only files that failed previously. Useful for iterative debugging; the doctester stores pass/fail status in timings2.json which is consulted.

rubrics_metrics.name: --initial / -i flag (show only first failure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only show the first failure in each doctest block to reduce noise from cascading failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --initial to avoid cascades of NameErrors/other follow-on failures making output hard to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: --show-skipped (show skipped optional tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Print a summary at the end of each file with the number of optional tests skipped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ./sage -t --show-skipped src/sage/rings/finite_rings/integer_mod.pyx prints counts of skipped axiom/cunningham/fricas/long/magma tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: --global-iterations and --file-iterations (repeating tests to find intermittent failures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run tests multiple times to search for intermittent 'Heisenbugs'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: --global-iterations N runs the whole set of tests N times serially; --file-iterations N runs tests within each file N times before proceeding. Useful for flaky failures; examples and sample outputs are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: --timeout / -T (adjust test timeout)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set a global timeout for tests; default may be insufficient on slow machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default timeout is 5 minutes; change with --timeout to avoid premature 'Timed out!' reports. Example: ./sage -tp 2 --all --timeout 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: --abspath (use absolute paths)
rubrics_metrics.description: Print filenames using absolute paths instead of relative paths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --abspath to make logs and error messages refer to absolute filenames, e.g. ./sage -t --abspath src/sage/doctest/control.py.

rubrics_metrics.name: --new (test changed files only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test files that have been modified or added since the last commit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful during development to run only changed files: ./sage -t --new. Example output shows doctesting only files changed since last git commit.

rubrics_metrics.name: --randorder (run tests in random order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run tests in a randomized order to reveal order-dependent bugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --randorder <seed> to randomize file order; note that tests within a given doctest block are still run in order. Example: ./sage -t --new --randorder 127.

rubrics_metrics.name: --force-lib (testing external non-package files)
rubrics_metrics.description: When testing a file not part of a package (no __init__.py), testing code loads globals from that file into the namespace; use --force-lib to disable this behaviour and require explicit imports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disable implicit loading when you want stricter import behaviour for standalone files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary logging (--logfile) and timings (--stats-path)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify a logfile and a JSON stats file storing timings and pass/fail status for each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --logfile to write a textual log and --stats-path to write timings2.json (default ~/.sage/timings2.json). The doctester reads timings2.json to sort files so slower tests run first to utilize multiple processes efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: --baseline-stats-path and known-test-failures.json
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish files with known doctest failures from new failures using a baseline stats file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare known-test-failures.json in the same format as timings2.json. Files marked as failed in baseline will be reported as '[failed in baseline]'; if only baseline failures exist, sage -t exits with status code 0. Use --baseline-stats-path to point to the baseline file.

rubrics_metrics.name: --installed and testing in virtual environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Test modules of Sage that are installed in a virtual environment using --installed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tox-created virtualenvs; example: pkgs/.../.tox/.../sage -t -p4 --installed. Note: installed copies (in site-packages/sage/...) should never be edited because they can be overwritten. doctest fixer can be run with --distribution/--venv/--environment to operate on installed distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest fixer (./sage --fixdoctests) purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Tool that runs doctester and replaces expected outputs of examples by the actual outputs from the current version of Sage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because this edits source files, best practice is to git commit beforehand and use git diff after to inspect automated edits. The fixer updates outputs and can normalize # optional/needs tags. It has many flags (e.g. --overwrite, --no-overwrite, --keep-both, --only-tags).

rubrics_metrics.name: --overwrite vs --no-overwrite (doctest fixer file write mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: --overwrite lets the doctest fixer edit source files; --no-overwrite writes new files with extension .fixed instead of overwriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you prefer not to allow automatic edits to the source, use --no-overwrite to inspect .fixed files first.

rubrics_metrics.name: --keep-both (preserve expected and actual outputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: When expected and actual outputs differ, duplicate the example marking two copies # optional - EXPECTED and # optional - GOT; both copies become optional and are not run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes --fixdoctests idempotent and is useful when you want to preserve both outputs for manual inspection; often used with --full-tracebacks to see full exception details.

rubrics_metrics.name: --full-tracebacks (disable traceback abbreviation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disable automatic abbreviation of tracebacks (the doctester normally uses .... to abbreviate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --full-tracebacks to preserve full exception details in output, especially useful combined with --keep-both to capture full actual traceback in the GOT copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: --only-tags (normalize only # optional/needs tags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the doctest fixer only take care of # optional/needs tags without changing expected results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable for mostly unattended runs where only tag normalization is desired, not output updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing # optional/needs FEATURE tags (style and automation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctest fixer removes redundant # optional/needs FEATURE tags, aligns tags on doctest lines, and suggests using block-scoped tags when tags are repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block-scoped tags are preferred over repeated per-doctest tags. The fixer also issues style warnings and will add or remove tags in many cases automatically. It aligns tags at fixed tab stops and will add missing # optional/needs tags if it detects doctest dataflow warnings (variable referenced only in optional doctest).

rubrics_metrics.name: --probe FEATURE (test optional/needs tags silently and remove if unnecessary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the doctest fixer probe examples marked # optional/needs FEATURE; if the example works without FEATURE, the tag is automatically removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probing is most effective when doctests do not reuse the same variable for different values. Use --probe FEATURE to clean up unneeded tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: --verbose for doctest fixer
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the doctest fixer show doctester messages one by one and report the changes made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to inspect what automated edits are being applied; combine with --no-overwrite or --keep-both for safer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual-environment mode behaviours and options (--distribution / --venv / --environment / --fixed-point)
rubrics_metrics.description: When running the doctest fixer for distributions/virtualenvs, the fixer will look up unknown global names in its own environment and add # needs tags; it will add ModuleNotFoundError tags automatically too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use --distribution to specify distributions to test; switches implied in this mode include --keep-both, --full-tracebacks, and --if-installed. --fixed-point runs distributions until no further changes are made. --venv and --environment allow more specific control.

rubrics_metrics.name: --long (ensure all doctests are updated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Force the doctest fixer to make sure that all doctests are updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes expected outputs are missed unless --long is used. Example: ./sage --fixdoctests --long --overwrite src/sage/arith/weird.py.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use git best-practices when editing doctests automatically
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the doctest fixer edits source files, commit changes beforehand and inspect diffs after running the fixer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended workflow: git commit your current changes, run ./sage --fixdoctests --overwrite, then use git diff to review automated edits. Alternatively use --no-overwrite to inspect .fixed files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reported timings are averages (caveat about timing data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported results for a file are the average time for all tests in that file to finish; a failure in a file is reported and testing proceeds with the next file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timings2.json contains these average times; use them for sorting to run slower tests earlier when parallelizing. Understand that per-file averages can mask per-test variance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Docker / containers for multi-platform testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Docker (or Docker-in-Docker via Codespaces) to run Sage builds and doctests across platforms; ensure the Docker client provides enough RAM (8 GB recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given for running ubuntu:latest, mounting source tree, installing build prerequisites (using Sage's build/pkgs/_prereq/distros/*.txt), generating Dockerfile via write-dockerfile.sh, and customizing docker build with build args (BASE_IMAGE, NUMPROC, EXTRA_CONFIGURE_ARGS, TARGETS_PRE/TARGETS). Use docker commit to save images and share with collaborators to reproduce bugs. If building in a container, note configure may require --enable-build-as-root or follow the configure message not to build as root.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Sage's database of distribution prerequisites and equivalent packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage contains files mapping required system package names per distribution (e.g. build/pkgs/_prereq/distros/debian.txt) and package equivalencies for SPKGs to system packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use build/bin/sage-guess-package-system and build/bin/sage-print-system-package-command to discover the package system and install commands; consult build/pkgs/<pkg>/distros/*.txt for equivalent system packages to avoid building SPKGs from source. Report configuration/system package lists when filing portability bug reports.
